established_findings.statement: Large language models are actively used to translate high-level intent or natural-language descriptions into network-configuration templates and code (intent→config), and prototype systems/benchmarks demonstrate this capability.
limitations: Many demonstrations are prototype-level or evaluated on curated tasks rather than broad production deployments
Performance varies by task complexity (basic BGP vs advanced multi-intent scenarios)

established_findings.statement: Architectures that augment LLM generation with deterministic validators, tool-augmented verification, or generate–validate–repair loops improve task correctness and reduce unsafe outputs relative to unconstrained LLM-only baselines in evaluated studies.
limitations: Improvements are reported on specific datasets and domains; gains and trade-offs (e.g., higher false refusals, latency) are context-dependent
Not all studies evaluate full end-to-end deployment risk in live networks

established_findings.statement: The literature contains multiple, convergent taxonomies documenting recurrent LLM failure modes (hallucination, epistemic/ calibration failures, sycophancy, drift, tool-orchestration failures) relevant to operational tasks.
limitations: Taxonomies synthesize observed behaviors but differ in granularity and experimental coverage
Some evidence is observational or limited-sample

established_findings.statement: Operational reliability in agentic NetOps/AIOps is driven strongly by the surrounding orchestration, assurance contracts, validators, sandboxing and rollback mechanisms rather than by LLM output quality alone.
limitations: Argumentative and survey-style evidence; quantitative comparisons of orchestration designs remain limited
Operational claims vary by domain and maturity of tooling

established_findings.statement: Agentic/agent-based NetOps evaluations and benchmarks exist but benchmark design and external validity are open concerns—benchmarks often do not fully capture deployment spectra or realistic failure conditions.
limitations: Benchmarks cited target specific domains/tasks (medical agents, CTI, NetConfEval) and may not generalize across all NetOps scenarios
Methodological critiques indicate risk of optimistic validity when datasets are not deployment-representative

established_findings.statement: Multi-signal or layered mitigation strategies (retrieval grounding, tool verification, constrained schemas, ensemble detection) reduce hallucination or unsupported outputs but introduce trade-offs (e.g., increased refusal rates, latency) documented in empirical studies.
limitations: Reported trade-offs depend on the precise controls and domains evaluated
Ensemble/mitigation systems require engineering effort and can increase complexity/latency

unresolved_questions.statement: Can tool-augmented, LLM-driven agents safely and reliably execute unmediated configuration changes in production NetOps at scale?
limitations: Reviews highlight a lack of strong production evidence for general-purpose autonomous action
Existing work emphasizes canary/rollback patterns rather than full autonomous production operation

unresolved_questions.statement: Which deterministic validators or verification toolchains (and what integration patterns) provide sufficient coverage for semantic correctness of generated network configs across diverse vendors and protocols?
limitations: Papers demonstrate validators or external models in limited settings; cross-vendor, multi-protocol validation comparisons are sparse in the supplied records

unresolved_questions.statement: How well do existing NetOps-oriented benchmarks predict real-world deployment risk (e.g., outage likelihood, rollback frequency) when used to evaluate agentic systems?
limitations: Direct empirical linking of benchmark scores to deployment incidents is not established in the provided records

unresolved_questions.statement: What are robust, standardized simulation/sandbox protocols and metrics for replayable safety evaluation and canary testing of LLM-driven NetOps agents?
limitations: Many works call for workflow-centred evaluation but a consolidated, standard protocol covering replay/canary/rollback is not present among the supplied records

unresolved_questions.statement: What is the longitudinal effect of model-generated content reentering training pipelines (epistemic decay) on NetOps-relevant corpora and how to prevent degradation of operational correctness over time?
limitations: The cited work models epistemic decay broadly; domain-specific empirical validation for NetOps corpora is not provided in the supplied records

candidate_gaps.statement: Lack of publicly available, standardized end-to-end NetOps agent benchmarks that include sandboxed execution, rollback/canary trials, and incident-like adversarial perturbations.
limitations: Multiple papers call for richer workflow-centred evaluation; some domain-specific benchmarks exist but not the comprehensive execution+rollback style benchmark requested

candidate_gaps.statement: Insufficient multi-vendor, protocol-diverse validation studies that quantify how well LLM-generated configurations satisfy semantic network properties across real equipment or high-fidelity emulators.
limitations: Existing work demonstrates template/config generation and some validation but often in limited protocol subsets or synthetic scenarios

candidate_gaps.statement: Limited empirical evidence on human–agent handoff strategies (when to escalate to operators) with quantified operational utility and reduced outage risk.
limitations: Surveys recommend escalation controls and assurance contracts but do not provide large-scale controlled evaluations of handoff thresholds

candidate_gaps.statement: Need for canonical provenance, evidence-scoring, and automated-judge protocols tailored to NetOps outputs to distinguish absence of evidence from evidence of absence when LLMs assert 'no issue' or 'reachability holds'.
limitations: Provenance and evidence-scoring frameworks exist in other domains; NetOps-specific operationalization and auditing protocols are not fully developed in supplied records

candidate_gaps.statement: Sparse production-grade case studies showing full autonomous NetOps agents executing live changes with measurable safety outcomes (e.g., demonstrated reduction in outages or verified rollback successes).
limitations: Reviews explicitly note that production evidence is substantial for detection/diagnosis but weak for general-purpose autonomous action

excluded_claims: LLMs are proven ready to autonomously perform live NetOps configuration changes in production without human oversight.
There is conclusive evidence in the supplied records that any single validator/tool eliminates all semantic or safety failures of LLM-generated configs across vendors/protocols.
Existing NetOps benchmarks reliably predict deployment safety metrics (e.g., outage rate) for autonomous agents without additional sandbox/canary evaluation.
Autonomous LLM agents introduce no trade-offs (latency, false refusals, added complexity) when layered with verification components.
